details:
Junior Astronaut: 3D Space Colony Simulator

Junior Astronaut is a browser-based game about building and managing a settlement on Mars or the Moon. Players lead a crew of four and try to keep everyone safe during a 30, 60, or 90 day mission. The game combines 3D base building, resource management, space science, and environmental emergencies.

At the start, players choose a destination. The Mars mission is set in Arcadia Planitia, where the colony must cope with a thin carbon dioxide atmosphere, cold temperatures, reduced sunlight, and dust storms. The Moon mission takes place near the South Pole, where there is almost no atmosphere, extreme temperature variation, radiation, and long periods when sunlight may be blocked by the terrain. The site displays facts about each location, including gravity, day length, temperature, sunlight, radiation, and distance from Earth.

Players build the colony by choosing modules from a construction menu and placing them on the base grid. Each structure has a purpose and costs materials. Solar arrays produce electricity, while battery banks store energy. Oxygen generators help supply breathable air, water recyclers recover water, and ice miners can collect water from suitable locations. Greenhouses produce food and some oxygen. Regolith shields provide protection, science labs generate research points, and communications dishes support cargo deliveries. A fission reactor can generate power when sunlight is unavailable.

The game tracks oxygen, water, food, energy, construction materials, science points, and crew health. Resource indicators show whether supplies are rising or falling, helping players decide what to build next. Good planning matters: power supports life-support equipment, food and water must last through the mission, and protective structures can help the base withstand hazards. Longer missions require more reliable production and backup systems.

During play, the colony may face dust storms, solar flares, meteorites, quakes, and freezing nights. These events can disrupt power, threaten the crew, or put pressure on supplies. Players can pause or change simulation speed while managing the base.

The main menu offers Demo mode, which guides players through a base tour, life-support science, a dust emergency, a NASA-related radiation alert, and a final report. A tutorial, Science Codex, and Mission Handbook provide additional guidance. The game also identifies NASA DONKI as a source for space-weather information about events such as solar flares and coronal mass ejections.

Overall, Junior Astronaut makes the challenges of living beyond Earth interactive. Players learn how a colony’s power, life-support, food, water, construction, and protection systems depend on one another while working to keep the crew alive.
